correctness.rationale: The four homogeneous harmonic subspaces are pairwise orthogonal and have the full degree-three dimension d(d-1)(d+4)/6. SO(d-1)-invariance reduces the cap operator to four scalar beta integrals; explicit normalizations and four polynomial factor identities determine every strict comparison and tie. In particular the squared-cap variable has Beta(1/2,(d-1)/2) law. The four factorizations show m=3 is always suboptimal and the only interior maximizer changes occur at 1/(d+2) and 3/(d+2). Exact rational checks for 104 dimensions plus independent quadrature at threshold values support the displayed all-symbolic proof but are not treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest published source, Simons–Dahlen arXiv:math/0603271v1, treats exactly the double-antipodal-cap domain on the ordinary two-sphere and derives general parity-separated low-pass spectral matrices, but the inspected result sections/appendices do not give two universal pure-degree-three crossings for every sphere dimension, their multiplicities, or complete optimal eigenspaces. Simons–Dahlen–Wieczorek arXiv:math/0408424v1 treats single-cap Slepian concentration and Bates–Khalid–Kennedy arXiv:1608.05479v1 concerns numerical high-band methods. General matrix computability in dimension three is not itself the all-dimension closed phase diagram. Related cubic-curvature and hemispherical-mask spectra concern non-equivalent operators. An unindexed direct result remains possible.
residual_risks: An unindexed analytical result on pure-degree-three concentration on antipodal caps or a stronger dimension-uniform branch-ordering theorem could make this a corollary.
The fixed-order matrices of Simons–Dahlen can reproduce d=3 instances, although no universal closed phase diagram is stated in the inspected sections.

value.rationale: The question asks which oscillatory cubic harmonic captures the most energy in a two-cap observation region, a central inverse-analysis invariant rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. A complete all-dimensional three-stage transition (quadrupolar transverse, meridional, zonal), a triple eigenvalue collision of multiplicity d(d+1)/2-1, and a second collision of multiplicity d are nontrivial structural information not supplied by general Slepian matrix existence. The exact thresholds can guide harmonic selection without diagonalizing matrices and provide sharp equality classifications. Higher pure degrees and unequal caps are not claimed.
